evals.prompt: Can you do an SEO audit of our SaaS website? We're getting about 2,000 organic visits/month but feel like we should be getting more. URL: https://example.com
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should ask clarifying questions about priority keywords, Search Console access, recent changes, and competitors. Should follow the audit framework priority order: Crawlability & Indexation, Technical Foundations, On-Page Optimization, Content Quality, Authority & Links. Should check robots.txt, XML sitemap, site architecture. Should evaluate title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, and content optimization. Should NOT report on schema markup based solely on web_fetch (must note the detection limitation). Output should follow the Audit Report Structure: Executive Summary, Technical SEO Findings, On-Page SEO Findings, Content Findings, and Prioritized Action Plan.
assertions: Checks for product-marketing.md
Asks clarifying questions about keywords, Search Console, recent changes
Follows audit priority order: crawlability first, then technical, on-page, content, authority
Checks robots.txt and XML sitemap
Evaluates title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure
Does NOT claim 'no schema found' based on web_fetch alone
Notes schema markup detection limitation
Output has Executive Summary
Output has Prioritized Action Plan
Each finding has Issue, Impact, Evidence, Fix, and Priority

evals.prompt: Why am I not ranking for 'project management software'? We have a page targeting that keyword but it's stuck on page 3.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on the casual 'why am I not ranking' phrasing. Should investigate both on-page and off-page factors. On-page: check title tag, H1, URL alignment with keyword; evaluate content depth vs competitors; check for keyword cannibalization. Technical: check indexation status, canonical tags, crawlability. Content quality: assess E-E-A-T signals, content depth, user engagement. Should provide specific, actionable fixes organized by priority. Should mention competitive analysis against current top-ranking pages.
assertions: Triggers on casual 'why am I not ranking' phrasing
Checks title tag, H1, URL alignment with target keyword
Evaluates content depth vs competitors
Checks for keyword cannibalization
Checks indexation status and canonical tags
Assesses E-E-A-T signals
Mentions competitive analysis against top-ranking pages
Provides actionable fixes organized by priority

evals.prompt: We just migrated from WordPress to Next.js and our organic traffic dropped 40% in the last month. Help!
evals.expected_output: Should route to references/site-moves.md, not the general audit framework. Should check the documented migration failure list: 302s instead of 301/308, redirect chains beyond 3 hops or loops, old URLs 404ing, many-to-one redirects to the homepage (soft 404 risk), development noindex or Disallow: / still live, canonicals still pointing at old URLs, internal links still pointing at old URLs, Change of Address not submitted (noting it is NOT needed for HTTP-to-HTTPS but IS needed per subdomain and www/non-www variant for a domain move), new sitemap not submitted, and a server unable to absorb the post-migration crawl surge. Should state Google's timing expectation: a medium-sized site takes a few weeks for most pages to move in the index, larger sites longer, and ranking fluctuation during that window is expected. Should state that 301 and other permanent redirects do not cause a loss in PageRank. Should cross-check against references/search-diagnostics.md so a coincident core update is not misattributed to the migration.
assertions: Routes to references/site-moves.md
Checks redirect type (301/308 not 302) and chain length
Checks for development noindex or Disallow left live on the new site
Checks canonicals and internal links point to new URLs
Checks Change of Address, and knows it is not needed for HTTP-to-HTTPS
Warns against many-to-one redirects to the homepage as a soft 404 risk
States 301 redirects do not lose PageRank
Gives Google's documented recovery timeline (weeks for medium sites)
Rules out a coincident core update before attributing the drop to the migration
Provides prioritized recovery plan

evals.prompt: Review the technical SEO of our e-commerce site. We have about 50,000 products and use faceted navigation.
evals.expected_output: Should route to references/ecommerce-seo.md. Should lead with faceted navigation crawl control: decide first whether facet URLs need to be indexed at all, then use robots.txt disallow patterns or URL fragments as the primary methods, noting Google calls rel=canonical and rel=nofollow 'generally less effective in the long term'. Should check whether category pages link to every product (Googlebot does not submit searches into a site search box) and recommend a sitemap or Merchant Center feed where they cannot. Should check pagination: unique URL per page, self-referencing canonical per page, never canonical page 2+ to page 1, no fragments for page numbers, and crawlable <a href> pagination beneath any infinite scroll or load-more. Should NOT flag shared titles/descriptions across paginated pages as a defect (explicitly permitted by Google) and should NOT flag missing rel=next/rel=prev (Google no longer uses them). Should confirm 50,000 products sits inside Google's stated crawl budget scope. Should mention product schema with the detection limitation caveat.
assertions: Routes to references/ecommerce-seo.md
Leads with faceted navigation crawl control
Prefers robots.txt or fragments over canonical/nofollow for facets
Checks that category pages link to all products; knows Googlebot does not use site search
Checks pagination has unique URLs and self-referencing canonicals per page
Does NOT flag shared titles/descriptions on paginated pages as a defect
Does NOT flag missing rel=next/rel=prev
Checks crawlable pagination beneath infinite scroll or load-more
Mentions product schema with detection limitation caveat
Findings include Impact ratings and specific fixes

evals.prompt: Can you check our blog posts for on-page SEO issues? We publish 4 posts per week but traffic has been flat for 6 months.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Content/Blog Sites framework: check for outdated content not refreshed, keyword cannibalization, missing topical clustering, poor internal linking, missing author pages. Should audit on-page elements: title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, keyword targeting per post. Should assess E-E-A-T signals for blog content. Should check for content depth issues and whether posts answer search intent. Should recommend a content audit process and provide a prioritized action plan for the existing content library.
assertions: Applies Content/Blog Sites framework
Checks for keyword cannibalization
Checks for topical clustering
Checks for internal linking quality
Audits title tags and meta descriptions without asserting a Google character limit
Does NOT recommend a word count target
Does NOT flag multiple H1s or skipped heading levels as SEO issues
Does NOT promise to improve an 'E-E-A-T score'
Does NOT recommend date-bumping as a freshness tactic
Assesses whether content answers search intent
Provides prioritized action plan

evals.prompt: I run a local plumbing business with 3 locations. My website barely shows up when people search for 'plumber near me' in our areas. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Local Business site-type framework. Should check for: inconsistent NAP (Name, Address, Phone) across the site, missing local schema markup (with detection limitation caveat), Google Business Profile optimization, missing individual location pages for each of the 3 locations, and missing local content. Should also check standard technical and on-page factors. Should recommend local-specific fixes: location-specific pages with unique content, local schema on each, GBP optimization, citation consistency.
assertions: Applies Local Business framework
Checks NAP consistency
Checks for local schema markup with detection caveat
Addresses Google Business Profile optimization
Recommends individual location pages for each location
Recommends local content strategy
Checks standard technical SEO factors too
Provides prioritized local SEO action plan

evals.prompt: Our site loads really slowly, especially on mobile. Pages take 5-6 seconds to load. Is this hurting our SEO?
evals.expected_output: Should focus on Core Web Vitals and cite the thresholds: LCP within 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1, noting INP replaced FID in March 2024. Should identify 5-6s as well above the LCP threshold. Should investigate TTFB, image optimization, JavaScript execution, CSS delivery, caching, CDN and font loading. Should recommend PageSpeed Insights, Lighthouse, WebPageTest and the Search Console Core Web Vitals report, and should NOT recommend the Mobile-Friendly Test or Mobile Usability report (both retired from Google's documentation in December 2023). Should state the ranking relationship accurately: Core Web Vitals are used by Google's ranking systems, but there is no single page experience signal and good scores do not guarantee top rankings. Should frame speed work as user experience with a ranking component, not as a ranking fix. Should cover the other page experience aspects Google names: HTTPS, mobile display, ad load, intrusive interstitials, main content distinguishable from the rest.
assertions: Cites correct CWV thresholds (LCP 2.5s, INP 200ms, CLS 0.1)
Identifies 5-6s as well above the LCP threshold
States there is no single page experience ranking signal
Does not claim good CWV guarantees rankings
Does NOT recommend the retired Mobile-Friendly Test or Mobile Usability report
Covers other page experience aspects (HTTPS, interstitials, ad load)
Investigates specific speed factors
Provides prioritized speed fixes

evals.prompt: I want to add FAQ schema to my product pages. Can you help me set that up?
evals.expected_output: Should NOT simply route to the schema skill. Should state that the FAQ rich result is retired: Google added a deprecation notice in May 2026, the feature stopped appearing on 7 May 2026, and the documentation was removed in June 2026. FAQPage markup is harmless but produces no rich result, so the work has no return. Should note the same applies to HowTo. Should then offer what is actually available for product pages from Google's current supported list - Product, product snippet, merchant listing, product variants, review snippet, shipping policy, return policy, loyalty program, breadcrumb - and route implementation of those to the schema skill. Should not invent a replacement feature.
assertions: States the FAQ rich result is retired and gives the May 2026 date
Explains FAQPage markup now produces no rich result
Notes HowTo is also retired
Offers currently supported alternatives relevant to product pages
Routes implementation of those types to the schema skill
Does not attempt a full SEO audit
Does not invent a replacement feature

evals.prompt: Our organic traffic fell about 35% starting three weeks ago. Nothing changed on the site that I know of. What happened?
evals.expected_output: Should treat this as a diagnosis, not an audit, and route to references/search-diagnostics.md. Should check the Search Console Data Anomalies page first to rule out a Google-side data or logging issue. Should read the clicks-vs-impressions pattern and explain what each pairing implies (impressions flat with clicks down points at title links and snippets, not rankings). Should work Google's six documented causes: technical issues, security issues, spam issues and manual actions, algorithmic update, seasonality and changing interests, and site moves. Should name the specific Search Console report per cause (Crawl stats, Page indexing, Security Issues, Manual Actions). Should apply the four Performance-report filters: 16-month date range for seasonality, period comparison across every tab, search type separation, and the Pages table sorted by Clicks Difference to establish blast radius. Should use Google Trends to separate a site-specific drop from a market-wide demand shift. If a core update is suspected, should apply the timing discipline: confirm the rollout finished on the Search Status Dashboard, wait a full week after completion, and compare that week to a week before the rollout started. Should not recommend quick fixes or content deletion as a first response.
assertions: Treats it as a diagnosis and routes to references/search-diagnostics.md
Checks Search Console Data Anomalies before assuming a site cause
Separates clicks from impressions and interprets the pattern
Works through Google's six documented causes
Names the specific Search Console report per cause
Applies the 16-month date range to test for seasonality
Uses the Pages table to establish blast radius (site-wide vs group vs single page)
Uses Google Trends to test whether demand moved market-wide
Applies core-update timing discipline (rollout complete, wait a week, compare pre-rollout)
Advises against quick fixes and against deleting content as a first response
